name: Pi Coding Agent
version_context: earendil-works/pi commit ede2c9b468d8e061c557d16957513715e6d49cd6 (official repository; current Pi package namespace at this revision)
summary: A minimal, extensible TypeScript agent harness composed of a provider-neutral model API, stateful tool-calling agent runtime, and coding-agent session layer with interactive, print, JSON, RPC, and SDK surfaces.
scope: pi-agent-core loop, messages, tools, and events
CLI, RPC, SDK, and package customization surfaces

features.name: Provider-neutral model boundary
features.description: The pi-ai package presents a unified multi-provider LLM API and model/auth registries beneath the agent runtime, while the repository README lists providers and the pi-agent-core package consumes the abstraction rather than a single vendor API.
benefits: Keeps agent-loop code reusable across provider transports
Allows model and credential selection to remain a replaceable boundary
costs: Provider-specific capabilities need compatibility and normalization
Model catalogs and authentication add another evolving contract

features.name: Evented tool-calling agent loop
features.description: pi-agent-core exposes agentLoop and a stateful Agent wrapper over an asynchronous loop that streams assistant responses, emits lifecycle events, queues steering and follow-up messages, validates tool arguments, and executes tool calls before continuation.
benefits: Separates orchestration events from presentation layers
Supports interruption, steering, follow-up, and programmatic consumers
costs: Queue modes and event ordering add state-machine complexity
Tool execution remains an authority boundary requiring caller policy

features.name: Persistent sessions with compaction and branching
features.description: The coding-agent session layer owns transcript state, model/thinking settings, tool loadouts, session switching and branching, compaction, retries, and export across interactive, print, RPC, and SDK modes.
benefits: Reuses one session abstraction across multiple I/O modes
Makes long-running conversations recoverable within the coding-agent layer
costs: Compaction and branch projections can change the context presented to a model
Session persistence and mode-specific UI behavior increase lifecycle surface

features.name: Extension, skill, prompt, theme, and package customization
features.description: The official README and extension types define a customization boundary for lifecycle subscriptions, LLM-callable tools, commands, keyboard/UI interactions, skills, prompt templates, themes, and distributable Pi packages.
benefits: Lets workflows add behavior without forking the core loop
Shares customization through documented package and extension surfaces
costs: Extensions can couple to event, tool, and UI contracts
Customization moves some correctness and permission policy to package authors

mathematical_views.question: How do prompts, assistant tool calls, tool results, steering messages, and follow-ups advance an agent context?
assumptions: An agent context is an ordered message sequence plus model, tool, and queue state
A provider stream returns an assistant message or an error/abort outcome
Tool execution and external side effects are abstracted as event-labeled transitions
The view describes inspected loop behavior and does not prove provider semantic equivalence

mathematical_views.model: Session projection and compaction state machine
mathematical_views.question: Which transcript, branch, compaction, retry, and mode states are visible to a coding-agent session?
assumptions: Session entries form an ordered history with branch and compaction projections
Compaction replaces or summarizes context according to the session policy
Interactive, print, JSON, RPC, and SDK modes share session state but differ in presentation
This is a candidate operational model, not a durability or correctness proof

mathematical_views.question: How do core lifecycle events, registered tools, commands, UI capabilities, skills, and packages compose around a session?
assumptions: Extensions are nodes connected to event, tool, command, and UI registration interfaces
Registration order and host mode constrain which edges are active
Package distribution is treated as an external deployment edge
Graph adjacency does not establish that an extension is safe or behavior-preserving

benefits: Reusable event stream for UI and automation
costs: Explicit queue and lifecycle ordering is required

benefits: Long-running sessions and multiple frontends share one abstraction
costs: Compaction and branching complicate context reasoning
Extension compatibility and policy become part of the integration surface
